name: Laru (North Sudan)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Schadeberg, Thilo C. (1981) A Survey of Kordofanian, vol. 1: The Heiban Group (phonological notes on Laru); no online copy reached

sources.citation: Schneider-Blum, G., B. Hellwig & T. C. Schadeberg (eds.). 2018. Nuba Mountain Language Studies - New Insights. Cologne: Köppe. / Schadeberg & Blench (eds.). 2013. Nuba Mountain Language Studies. Cologne: Köppe.
sources.note: Publisher tables of contents read online: no chapter on Laru in either volume (Heiban chapters cover Moro, Koalib, Ebang only).

sources.citation: Kuku, Nabil Abdalla. 2012. Laru Vowel Harmony. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 10: 17-34. Juba: SIL.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (0 hits for 'stress' in the whole volume). Section 4 'Tone' (p. 21) states Laru has two level tones (H, L) and two contour tones (HL, LH); at most two tones per vowel in 1-2 syllable words, one tone per vowel in words of 3+ syllables; grammatical tone present but not yet analysed.
Nothing on stress; phonology section is paraphrased from Kuku 2012/2015. Useful only because it supplied the direct SIL reapdata URLs for OPSL 10 and 11.

sources.citation: Kuku, Nabil Abdalla. 2015. Laru Locatives. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 11: 1-16. Juba: SIL.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (0 hits for 'stress' in the volume). Section 1.5 'Tone' (p. 3) repeats the H/L/HL/LH inventory and adds that both lexical and grammatical tone contrasts exist (citing Abdalla 2013); the introduction (p. 1) states the description is of the Yilaru dialect.
